title: Derived base-change maps compose along stacked cartesian squares
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphisms of schemes and let $m:Z'\to Z$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Form $Y'=Y\times_ZZ'$ with projections $l:Y'\to Y$ and $g':Y'\to Z'$, and $X'=X\times_YY'$ with projections $k:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]; then $X'$, with $k$ and $g'\circ f'$, is a fibre product of $g\circ f$ and $m$. Write $\beta^{\mathrm{top}}_E:Ll^*Rf_*E\to Rf'_*Lk^*E$, $\beta^{\mathrm{bot}}_M:Lm^*Rg_*M\to Rg'_*Ll^*M$ and $\beta^{\mathrm{out}}_E:Lm^*R(g\circ f)_*E\to R(g'\circ f')_*Lk^*E$ for the canonical derived base-change maps of the upper square, the lower square and the outer rectangle [def-pc-derived-base-change-map, def-pc-derived-pullback, def-pc-derived-direct-image], and $\rho:R(g\circ f)_*\simeq Rg_*Rf_*$, $\rho':R(g'\circ f')_*\simeq Rg'_*Rf'_*$ for the canonical composition isomorphisms [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-composition]. Then for every $E$ in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category], for which $Rf_*E$ lies in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-preserves-qcoh],
$$\rho'_{Lk^*E}\circ\beta^{\mathrm{out}}_E=Rg'_*(\beta^{\mathrm{top}}_E)\circ\beta^{\mathrm{bot}}_{Rf_*E}\circ Lm^*(\rho_E).$$
No Tor independence, flatness, properness or invertibility of any base-change map is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0ATL (remark-compose-base-change): the base change maps of the two stacked squares compose to the base change map of the outer rectangle; the verification is omitted there. Restricted here to quasi-compact quasi-separated f, g so that the canonical map of def-pc-derived-base-change-map is defined on the intermediate object.

proof.text: The outer square is cartesian directly from the universal properties: maps $a:T\to X$, $b:T\to Z'$ with $gfa=mb$ first determine the unique $y:T\to Y'$ with $ly=fa$, $g'y=b$, and then the unique $x:T\to X'$ with $kx=a$, $f'x=y$. Uniqueness follows in the same order. Put $P_h=Lh^*$ and $S_h=Rh_*$. Since $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, $M=S_fE$ has quasi-coherent cohomology, so both the top map at $E$ and the bottom map at $M$ are in the domain of the stated definition.

proof.text: Use the canonical composition isomorphisms $\kappa$ of [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-composition] to identify composites of the $S_h$; these are the comparisons for the derived direct images of [def-pc-derived-direct-image], characterized by the right-derived unit equation, and they are the comparisons used in [def-pc-derived-base-change-map]. Their reassociations are coherent by [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-composition-associativity]: for three composable morphisms of schemes, the two ways of passing from $S_{hgf}$ to $S_hS_gS_f$, with the transport along associativity of scheme morphisms, agree at every derived object. Thus write $S_fS_k=S_lS_{f'}$, $S_gS_l=S_mS_{g'}$, $S_{gf}=S_gS_f$, and $S_{g'f'}=S_{g'}S_{f'}$ while retaining the canonical comparisons. Concretely the first square comparison is $\kappa_{l,f'}\kappa_{f,k}^{-1}$ after the equality transport along $fk=lf'$; the second is $\kappa_{m,g'}\kappa_{g,l}^{-1}$ after $gl=mg'$, and the outer one $S_{gf}S_k\simeq S_mS_{g'f'}$ is defined in the same way after $gfk=mg'f'$. Equality transports are natural, so the associativity law for $(k,f,g)$, $(f',l,g)$ and $(f',g',m)$ identifies the outer comparison, conjugated by $\rho$ and $\rho'$, with the composite $S_gS_fS_k\simeq S_gS_lS_{f'}\simeq S_mS_{g'}S_{f'}$ of $S_g$ of the first square comparison and the second square comparison at $S_{f'}$; the middle comparison $S_gS_{lf'}$ cancels with its inverse. This justifies all the identifications in the next two steps without asserting strict equality of chosen derived functors.

proof.text:
Write $\eta_h:1\to S_hP_h$ for the unit of $P_h\dashv S_h$, and abbreviate $B=\beta^{\mathrm{top}}_E$ and $A=\beta^{\mathrm{bot}}_{S_fE}$. By the defining unit formula for base change, the adjuncts of these maps are, in the coherent notation of Step 2,
$$S_l(B)\circ\eta_{l,S_fE}=S_f(\eta_{k,E}),\qquad S_m(A)\circ\eta_{m,S_gS_fE}=S_g(\eta_{l,S_fE}).$$
For example the first equation is an equality from $S_fE$ to $S_lS_{f'}P_kE$; the right side includes the comparison $S_fS_k\simeq S_lS_{f'}$. These equations are the forward/inverse cancellation of the adjunction Hom bijections, not an assertion that $A$ or $B$ is invertible.

source.place: Tag 0ATL, remark-compose-base-change; explicit verification using the unit definition of base change and Tag 0D5T

proof.text:
Take the adjunct under $P_m\dashv S_m$ of $S_{g'}(B)\circ A$. Its source is $S_gS_fE$ and its target is $S_mS_{g'}S_{f'}P_kE$. Functoriality and the two equations in Step 3 give
$$\begin{aligned}
S_mS_{g'}(B)\circ S_m(A)\circ\eta_m
&=S_mS_{g'}(B)\circ S_g(\eta_l)\\
&=S_g\bigl(S_l(B)\circ\eta_l\bigr)\\
&=S_gS_f(\eta_k).
\end{aligned}$$
In the middle equality the comparison $S_mS_{g'}\simeq S_gS_l$ is natural at the morphism $B$. By the defining unit formula, the adjunct of $\beta^{\mathrm{out}}_E$ is $S_{gf}(\eta_{k,E})$ followed by the outer comparison $S_{gf}S_k\simeq S_mS_{g'f'}$ of Step 2. Hence the adjunct of $\rho'_{P_kE}\circ\beta^{\mathrm{out}}_E$ is $S_m(\rho'_{P_kE})$ after it, while by naturality of $\eta_m$ at $\rho_E$ the adjunct of $S_{g'}(B)\circ A\circ P_m(\rho_E)$ is the displayed composite after $\rho_E$. Naturality of $\rho$ at $\eta_{k,E}$ and the identification of comparisons at the end of Step 2 show that these two adjuncts are equal. The Hom bijection is injective, so the two maps agree. Restoring the comparisons gives
$$\rho'_{P_kE}\circ\beta^{\mathrm{out}}_E=S_{g'}(\beta^{\mathrm{top}}_E)\circ\beta^{\mathrm{bot}}_{S_fE}\circ P_m(\rho_E).$$
Only the composition comparisons were inverted; no base-change morphism was inverted.
